title: Fix your Mistake!
reviewNotes: Montage, captions and native complete later boards reviewed. Two separate complete eight-piece later variations begin after ...Kxg7 at 62 seconds and after ...Qxg7 at 66 seconds. Rg2+ is proved against all four king replies through exact seven-piece outcomes after Rxg8. Re8+ is proved against both Qg8 and Qf8, followed by the corresponding queen capture. Representative king retreats and the omitted Qf8 block are explicitly independent. The original Ng7 choice, Nf6/Qg1 stalemate trap and Nh5 recovery are source context outside this selected proof. All a4/c4/f7/h7 pawns are preserved.
transcript: You cannot change the past, but sometimes mistakes can be fixed. In this position, white is trying to get this queen off the board. And one move that comes to [music] mind is knight to f6 because if the queen moves, for example, to g3 after rook to e8 check and king g7, there's going to be knight h5 fork picking up the queen and winning the game. If the queen stays on this line, this is simply going to be a fork with the king. But unfortunately, black has the incredible move queen to G1. And now after rook to H8 check, king G7, even if we go for this skewer, black has an incredible resource with king to H6. And now if we take the queen, this is simply going to be a stalemate and a draw. So knight to F6 doesn't work. The winning move is knight to G7. A beautiful little trap. Anything that is not taking the knight simply allows this skewer. And now after the queen takes, the knight is actually going to be able to stop both pawns and we're [music] going to be able to promote our own pawn. If the king takes, we simply have a skewer. We pick up the queen and we promote. And if the queen takes, we have rook E8 check. This would almost be a checkmate. The queen has to block. [music] And now it's the same thing. But wait, if you played knight to F6 and allowed queen to G1, you can still win this game if you simply go back to H5. And there is no easy way to stop it for black. If the king tries to create an escape now, the skewer does work. There is no stalemate trap. We pick up the [music] queen and we win the game. There is no way for black to defend the E8 square, which is the checkmating square, meaning that the queen will have to go back to G8 to desperately try and defend E8. But now we can fix our mistakes and go knight to G7 and win the game. If you love incredible chess, follow for
